title: VoltAde buys GritBar? A sports-nutrition deal
prompt: Our client is VoltAde, a sports-drink brand. It is thinking about buying GritBar, a fast-growing protein-bar startup. VoltAde's CEO asks: does this deal make sense?

clarifying_answers.objective: Grow beyond drinks into sports nutrition; the deal should add profit within two years.
clarifying_answers.deal: VoltAde would buy 100% of GritBar for cash.

hidden_facts.fact: GritBar has $40M of revenue, growing 30% a year, with a 10% operating margin.

hidden_facts.hint: the price or what the founders want

hidden_facts.fact: VoltAde sells in 20,000 gyms and convenience stores; GritBar sells in 5,000. Putting GritBar in VoltAde's outlets could add $12M of revenue in year one.
Surveys say 60% of GritBar buyers also drink sports drinks, and VoltAde is their favorite brand.
Integration would cost about $5M one time. GritBar uses a contract manufacturer, so there are no factories to merge.

math_answers.question: What revenue multiple are the founders asking?
What would GritBar's revenue be next year, including the distribution boost?
What operating profit would that bring at today's margin?

ideal_structure: Target standalone value: growth and margins
recommendation: Yes. The customers overlap heavily (60% of GritBar buyers drink sports drinks) and VoltAde can put GritBar into 4 times as many outlets. With the distribution boost, GritBar could reach about $64M of revenue and $6.4M of operating profit next year. 3x revenue is reasonable for 30% growth, and integration is cheap at $5M. Keep the founders through an earn-out.
common_mistakes: Judging the price on today's profit only
Not putting a number on the distribution synergy
